newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian prosecutor seeks to indict Prodi - reports.
newsitem.headline: Italian prosecutor seeks to indict Prodi - reports.

text.p: An Italian magistrate has asked for Prime Minister Romano Prodi to be charged with complicity in abuse of office over dealings when he was chairman of state holding IRI, the news agency ANSA reported on Monday.

It said the request to indict Prodi and other Italians who were board members of IRI in 1993 related to the sale by the giant holding company of the food unit Cirio and had been lodged by Rome deputy public prosecutor Giuseppe Geremia.
IRI sold 62 percent of Cirio to Fis.Vi, a consortium of cooperatives, in October 1993, according to published reports.
Prodi, appointed prime minister last May at the head of a centre-left government, was not immediately available for comment but has said previously that the sale was in order.
The AGI news agency said Geremia's request alleged that Fis.Vi had gained an "unjust advantage" in its purchase of Cirio as a result of actions by the IRI board of Prodi and five others.

AGI said the indictment would be considered by examining judge Edoardo Landi, who must decide whether to issue formal charges against Prodi and the five others and commit them for trial. Landi can also decide there are no grounds to proceed.
